battle.name: 漢平東越之戰
battle.brief: 建元三年秋，征側、征貳在交趾起兵反漢，殺太守、司馬，據雒城、九真。武帝遣伏波將軍路博德率師南下，自南海番禺經湘水、靈渠、灕水抵蒼梧，再沿紅水河進軍交趾，歷三年而平。卡面月牙劍是埃及新王國的單刃彎鉤劍，此役並未使用，只作為東越土著柳葉形銅劍的形制對照。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰的一方是西漢朝廷及其在南方的附庸南越國。建元三年（公元前140年）秋，漢武帝以朝廷名義出師，名義上的對象是交趾、九真、合浦三郡；實際作戰時，兵員由長沙、零陵、桂陽、南海等郡徵發，多為編戶齊民中被徵發的南方郡縣卒，另有熟悉山水的巴蜀與南越本地吏卒充當嚮導與行舟者。需要注意的一點是，漢軍開拔之時交趾仍由南越國的官署治理，漢廷出兵同時夾帶著帝國邊疆政策：南越王趙眜與漢使往來交涉，漢軍指揮層既要平叛，也要維持南越王室的合法性，因此整場戰役自始就是一場軍事行動與外交操作交疊的雙重工程。另一方是起兵反抗的交趾本地勢力，核心是征側、征貳姊妹（Trưng Trắc、Trưng Nhị）及其宗族、鄉里武裝，據有交趾郡治雒城與九真郡全境，並一度把勢力伸入合浦郡的沿海縣份，其作戰依託的是熟悉丘陵、溪澗與叢林的本地部曲，而非任何常備大軍。
countriesEn: One side was the Western Han court together with its southern client state of Nanyue. In the autumn of the third year of Jianyuan (140 BCE), Emperor Wu of Han dispatched troops in the name of the court, nominally against the three commanderies of Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Hepu. In practice the manpower was drawn from the commanderies of Changsha, Lingling, Guiyang and Nanhai, mostly southern registered households conscripted into the provincial levies, together with local Nanyue and Bashu officials and boatmen who knew the mountains and the waterways. It should be noted that when the Han army set out, Jiaozhi was still administered by the authorities of the Nanyue kingdom, and the Han expedition carried a second purpose, namely imperial frontier policy: the king of Nanyue, Zhao Mo, corresponded with Han envoys, and the Han command had both to suppress the revolt and to uphold the legitimacy of the Nanyue royal house. From the outset the campaign was therefore a military operation entangled with diplomacy. The other side was the local Jiaoji power that rose in revolt, centred on the sisters Zheng Ce and Zheng E (Trưng Trắc, Trưng Nhị), their clan and village levies, holding the commandery seat of Luocheng and the whole of Jiuzhen, and at one point pushing into the coastal counties of Hepu. Their strength lay not in any standing army but in local bands who knew the hills, the streams and the forest.
people: 征側與征貳是姊妹，出身樅陽（今越南前江省美拖一帶），其先世為蜀郡移民，後在交趾落地生根，家世為本地豪族，征側又嫁與交趾太守士燮之子，藉婚姻與宗族網絡掌握人手與財貨，是起事的發動者與象徵人物。漢廷方面的關鍵人物是伏波將軍路博德，他是漢武帝為此役任命的統帥，奉命自內地率師南下，負責統籌水陸兩路的推進；漢武帝劉徹則是決策者，下詔發兵、調發各郡兵糧並維持與南越王室的交涉。交趾本地的郡太守、司馬等漢朝官員在起事中被殺，越地其他郡縣的官吏則多數按兵不動或倒向叛方，這種分化說明地方社會的選擇並非一致。史籍方面，主要記錄此役的是《漢書·南越傳》《漢書·武帝紀》以及後出的《後漢書·南蠻西南夷列傳》，三者的年代與地名可互相比勘，而具體指揮細節多已散佚，只能由零星記載推想。
peopleEn: Zheng Ce and Zheng E were sisters, born in Tùng Âng (present-day Mỹ Tho in Tiền Giang province, Vietnam), whose ancestors had migrated from the commandery of Shu and settled in Jiaozhi. Their family was locally powerful, and Zheng Ce had married the son of the governor of Jiaozhi, Shi Xie, giving her access through marriage and kinship networks to both men and wealth; she was the spark of the revolt and its most enduring symbol. On the Han side the key figure was the General of the Waves, Lu Bodu, appointed by Emperor Wu to command the expedition and to coordinate the advance by water and by land out of the interior. The decision to send the army, to requisition men and grain from the commanderies, and to manage relations with the Nanyue royal house belonged to Emperor Wu Liu Che himself. The Han-appointed governor and military commandant of Jiaozhi were killed when the revolt broke out, while officials in the other commanderies of the region mostly stayed put or joined the rebels, which shows that local society did not choose unanimously. The principal records of the campaign are the Account of Nanyue and the Annals of Emperor Wu in the Book of Han, together with the later Treatise of the Southern Barbarians in the Book of Later Han; the dates and place names of the three can be compared against one another, but most of the operational detail has been lost and can only be inferred from scattered notices.
kits: 本卡月牙劍是埃及新王國時代約公元前1500年已成熟的單刃彎鉤劍，形制外彎、刃口內凹、砍入肉體後不易拔出，既可作兵器也常作儀仗；此役之中它並未出現，戰場上沒有任何一件可以對號入座的武器與之相當。真正投入戰鬥的是雙方各自的冷兵器：漢軍以環首刀、直身雙刃劍為主要佩刀，輔以長矛、戈形兵器、弓、臂弩與蹶張弩等射擊器械，護具為蒙皮盾、楯牌以及皮甲、札甲一類的札葉披甲，長兵器以木杆安刃的矛為主，重裝兵員極少；水軍則有樓船、戈船、走舸等不同船型，專司在河道中承接側翼衝擊與投射火矢、落石。東越一方多靠本地青銅器：圓莖、菱形格、圓形莖首的柳葉形銅劍，各型短匕首，銅斧與農具改製的器械，竹木削成的矛、盾，石鏃與骨鏃箭矢，以及銅鼓、干欄式高腳建築一類的聚落設施。值得對照的是，月牙劍那種「一擊即退、不與人纏鬥」的實用邏輯，在交趾出土的短兵刃上同樣看得到：一來青銅刃口弧度小、便於在狹窄地形中抽砍，二來銅料珍貴，能鑄成劍已足以立威，無須追求如青銅時代早期那樣的厚刃重身。
kitsEn: The khopesh on this card is a single-edged curved sickle sword already mature in Egypt by about 1500 BCE, its blade bending outward with an incurved edge so that it could be driven home and not easily withdrawn; it served both as a weapon and as an item of ceremony. It did not appear in this campaign, and nothing on the battlefield corresponds to it. The cold weapons actually used were the two sides' own. The Han army carried ring-pommel sabres and straight double-edged swords as its principal side arms, supported by spears, halberd-like polearms, bows, crossbows of the single-arm and sprung-tension types, and used hide-covered shields, mantlets and hide or lamellar armour, with spears on wooden hafts as the main close-order weapon and armoured heavy infantry in very small numbers. Its river force had several hull types, including tower-ships, war galleys and light fast boats, used to deliver flank attacks and to shoot arrows and stones from the waterways. The eastern Yue side relied largely on local bronze: willow-leaf swords with a round tang, a lozenge-shaped guard and a disc-shaped pommel, short daggers of several types, bronze axes and tools adapted as weapons, spears and shields of bamboo and wood, and arrowheads of stone and bone, together with bronze drums and pile-dwelling settlements. The comparison worth making is that the same practical logic seen in the khopesh, one blow and withdraw rather than prolonged duelling, is visible in the short blades excavated at Jiaozhi: the bronze edges have a slight curve that suits hacking in narrow ground, and bronze was so costly that a sword cast at all was already a statement of authority, so there was no need to chase the heavy and deep section of the earlier Bronze Age.
tactics: 漢軍的戰術核心是水陸並行、溯流而上。因交趾腹地的交通靠河道，漢廷的推進路線是先由南海郡番禺一線出師，經湘水北上，入零陵、桂陽一帶，再借秦代開鑿的靈渠轉入灕水，抵蒼梧郡（今梧州）設營，之後沿西江、紅水河一路南下，直至交趾郡治雒城；沿途設營、屯糧，兵船分列於干支河道，主力則集中於決戰地域。前進次序是典型的先點後面：先取郡治雒城以奪政治中樞與水陸樞紐，再分兵掃清九真郡內陸山地，斷絕城鄉之間的往來，最後以搜索、封鎖與勦殲三種手段並行收束殘部。追擊一段有浪井、荒波、麊泠等地名，大致落在交趾郡治以北的紅水河與馬江流域，可見漢軍曾經把戰線推進到叛軍預想的山地縱深。叛軍的應對則以地利為主：憑藉丘陵、叢林與水險，避開漢軍的弩陣與水軍正面優勢，游擊各處、破壞歸附政權的鄉里堡障，待漢軍主力移動再聚合反擊，漢軍因此被迫分兵、延長糧道，而糧秣自長沙、桂陽沿湘水轉運、經靈渠與灕水一段逐段接力的後勤安排，成為漢軍真正的弱點。
tacticsEn: The tactical core of the Han army was movement by water and land together, advancing upstream. Because transport in the heart of Jiaozhi depended on rivers, the Han route ran from the Nanhai commandery and Panyu up the Xiang River, into the Lingling and Guiyang region, then through the Lingqu canal cut under the Qin into the Li River, where a base was established at Cangwu (present-day Wuzhou). From there the force moved down the Xijiang and the Red River until it reached Luocheng, the seat of Jiaozhi commandery. Camps and supply depots were established along the line, war boats were distributed across the tributaries, and the main body was concentrated in the decisive zone. The sequence of operations followed the classic pattern of taking the key point first and the periphery afterwards: Luocheng was seized to win the political and riverine hub, the force was then split to sweep the interior hills of Jiuzhen, cutting the roads between town and country, and the last stage relied on search, blockade and destruction in parallel to close out the surviving bands. The pursuit stage carries the place names Langjing, Huangbo and Miling, located roughly in the Red River and Ma River basins north of the Jiaozhi seat, showing that the Han pushed the battle into the mountainous depth the rebels had counted on. The rebels answered with terrain: they took the hills, the forest and the water crossings, avoided the Han crossbow formations and the river fleet head-on, raided the villages of communities that had submitted, and re-concentrated to strike when the Han main body moved off. The Han were therefore forced to disperse and to lengthen their supply line, and the real weakness of the Han army lay in its logistics, with grain moving from Changsha and Guiyang along the Xiang River and handed over in relay stages across the Lingqu and Li sections.
data: 這場戰爭留下來的數字多屬概略之數，只宜作量級參考。兵員方面，漢廷調發的兵數常被概括為以萬計，《漢書》記各郡奉詔發兵、郡兵隨軍，總數當在數萬之譜；分路兵額沒有可靠記載。叛軍方面，郡兵與鄉里武裝整體加入，起事之初即取得交趾郡治與九真郡，兵源來自被徵發的本地民戶，人數同樣以數萬計。戰果方面，決戰中漢軍斬首以萬計、捕獲首虜與男女以千計，不同傳本之間的數目略有出入，應視為概數而非精確統計。距離上，自番禺到交趾郡治，水路約二千餘里，其中溯湘水入灕水一段便需數百里，最後的搜捕戰深入九真內陸山地，縱深數百里，糧道相應被拉長。時間上，自建元三年（公元前140年）秋起事，到建元五年（公元前138年）肅清，前後約三年。兵種比例上可以推知弩手與長矛手合計佔多數，騎兵比例極低，因為嶺南水網密布、馬匹缺乏，且行軍受季風與颱風影響，多在水位較低的季節在河道中推進。以上除時間跨度與水路里程可由地理與紀年推算外，其餘多出自史籍的概括敘述。
dataEn: The numbers that survive for this campaign are largely general estimates and should be read only as orders of magnitude. On troops, the Han levy is conventionally described as numbering in the tens of thousands, the Book of Han recording that the commanderies obeyed the edict and sent their provincial levies; no reliable figure survives for the individual columns. On the rebel side, the commandery soldiers and village bands joined wholesale, and the movement took the seat of Jiaozhi and the whole of Jiuzhen at the outset, drawing its men from the conscripted local households, again in the tens of thousands. On results, the Han are said to have cut down heads by the tens of thousands and to have taken prisoners and captives by the thousand, with the figures varying slightly between recensions; they should be treated as approximations rather than exact statistics. On distance, the water route from Panyu to the seat of Jiaozhi runs to more than two thousand li, of which the stretch climbing the Xiang and Li rivers alone accounts for several hundred, while the final search-and-destroy fighting went deep into the interior hills of Jiuzhen over a depth of several hundred li, stretching the supply line accordingly. On time, the revolt began in the autumn of the third year of Jianyuan (140 BCE) and was suppressed in the fifth year (138 BCE), roughly three years in all. On composition, crossbowmen and spearmen together must have made up the great majority, with a very small proportion of cavalry, since the southern river network is dense, horses are scarce, and campaigning along the rivers was constrained by the monsoon and by typhoons, which pushed movement into the drier seasons when the channels could be navigated. Apart from the duration and the water distances, which can be calculated from geography and from the reign chronology, the rest come from the general statements of the historical texts.
cause: 起事的直接原因，是漢朝在交趾、九真、合浦三郡的治理方式激起本地社會的整體反感。這三郡在趙佗建南越之後長期為南越國的內地，漢廷於其地設置太守、司馬、巡查御史等官，把中原的編戶、賦役與刑罰體系強加於當地；史書所記的具體情形，是官吏在征收與贓賂上極為苛刻，郡中民戶不堪其擾，而征側、征貳所出的豪族之家在嫁娶、蔭庇、輸納等方面與官府長期角力，一旦遇上郡吏索求無厭，衝突便迅速激化。姐妹二人殺死郡太守與司馬、奪取郡兵之後，局勢失控的原因有兩層：其一是九真、合浦等地的官吏與鄉里響應，叛軍很快取得郡級以上的統治權；其二是南越國王室的處境微妙，呂嘉為相、把持朝政，漢廷若不加兵，則交趾一旦脫離郡縣體系，南越的內政與漢的邊疆安排都會失衡。於是漢武帝在交趾尚屬南越統治的狀態下出兵，戰爭在名義上是討平叛亂，在結構上卻是漢朝把南越內地重新收編為郡縣的第一次軍事嘗試。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the rising was a general revulsion in local society against the way the Han administered the three commanderies of Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Hepu. These territories had been the interior of the Nanyue kingdom since Zhao Tuo founded it, and the Han court had set up governors, commandants and travelling inspectors there, imposing the Central Kingdom's household registration, corvée and penal system on the district. The historical texts describe the specifics bluntly: the officials were extortionate in their levies and their bribes, and the registered households of the commandery could no longer endure the pressure. The clan from which Zheng Ce and Zheng E came was a powerful local family, used to bargaining with the authorities over marriage, patronage and remittance, and once a commandery official demanded more than the clan could pay, the conflict turned violent. After the sisters killed the commandery governor and the commandant and seized the provincial troops, the situation ran out of control for two reasons. First, officials and villages in Jiuzhen and Hepu answered the rising, and the insurgents quickly held authority at commandery level and above. Second, the position of the Nanyue royal house was delicate, with Lü Jia the chancellor dominating the court, and if Han troops did not march, then a Jiaozhi that slipped out of the commandery system would have destroyed both the internal order of Nanyue and the Han frontier settlement. Wu therefore sent troops while Jiaozhi was still formally under Nanyue: nominally a punitive expedition against rebels, structurally the first military attempt by the Han to absorb the interior of Nanyue back into the commandery system.
impact: 最直接的後果，是交趾自建元五年起徹底回到漢朝的直接管轄之下，郡縣建置重新編訂，叛軍降眾被收編或徙置，郡兵由漢朝的編制重建，郡內的產糧、徵賦與治安秩序重整，這套安排在此後數十年裡逐步定型，日後演為交州刺史部的基礎。更大的長尾效應出現在十餘年後：南越國相呂嘉的反叛與漢廷的介入，最終導致元鼎六年（公元前111年）漢滅南越，嶺南全境入漢，設交趾、南海、合浦、蒼梧、鬱林、桂林、甌等郡，元封年間再置交州刺史部。若沒有建元三年以來對交趾用兵所確立的郡縣秩序與水陸通道，公元前111年的遠征將缺少落腳點與補給線。就兵器與戰術而言，漢式環首刀、臂弩與樓船在嶺南確立了長期優勢，越式柳葉形銅劍逐步退居禮器與象徵的位置，銅鼓與干欄式聚落則被記錄為東越的物質標誌。政治記憶上，這場戰役在中國與越南兩套史觀中長期存在張力：越南史書視征側為民族英雄與反抗的先驅，近代民族主義論述屢屢徵引；中國學界則強調它是統一多民族國家在嶺南形成過程中的一環，同時承認其鎮壓叛亂的性質。
impactEn: The most direct effect was that Jiaozhi returned completely to direct Han administration from the fifth year of Jianyuan: the commandery and county structure was rewritten, rebel prisoners and surrenders were enrolled or relocated, the provincial troops were rebuilt on a Han footing, and the fiscal, corvée and security order of the district was reorganised. That arrangement hardened over the following decades and later became the basis of the Jiaozhou provincial inspectorate. The longer tail came a dozen years later, when the revolt of Lü Jia and the Han intervention culminated in the destruction of Nanyue in the sixth year of Yuanding (111 BCE), bringing the whole of Lingnan into the empire with the commanderies of Jiaozhi, Nanhai, Hepu, Cangwu, Yulin, Guilin and Ou, followed by the establishment of the Jiaozhou inspection circuit in the Yuanfeng era. Without the county order and the water routes fixed by the campaign begun in 140 BCE, the expedition of 111 BCE would have had neither a base nor a supply line. In terms of arms and tactics, Han ring-pommel sabres, crossbows and river craft took a lasting hold in the south, the willow-leaf bronze swords of the Yue receded towards the position of ceremonial and symbolic objects, and the bronze drums and pile dwellings were recorded as the material markers of the eastern Yue. In political memory the campaign has long carried tension between two historiographies: Vietnamese texts treat Zheng Ce as a national heroine and a pioneer of resistance, and modern nationalist discourse has repeatedly invoked her, while Chinese scholarship stresses the campaign as one stage in the formation of a unified multi-ethnic state in Lingnan while accepting its character as the suppression of a rebellion.
result: 平叛最終以漢軍的勝利告終。征側、征貳的聯軍在雒城、九真一線接戰後崩潰，漢軍追奔至浪井、荒波、麊泠一帶再戰，叛軍主力被殲於山區與河谷之間，殘部退入叢林；史籍記征貳兵敗後自殺，征側則不知所終，或云被擒獲，或云終身隱匿於山林。建元五年（公元前138年），九真郡境內最後的抵抗被肅清，郡縣官署得以重設，戰役以漢朝重新掌握交趾、九真、合浦三郡的行政與軍事控制告終。從帝國的角度看，這場戰爭的結果是一次成功的邊疆收復：漢廷以最少的駐軍換得了對嶺南內地的長期經營權，四年後完成的南越平定讓這次收復變成制度化的編郡設州；從交趾本地社會的角度看，結果則是一次舊有秩序的崩解與重建，豪族主導的武裝被解散，郡兵被納入漢朝編制，此後數百年間，漢朝的郡縣官署與南越的宗族社會在交趾長期共存、互相借重，也長期互相衝突。
resultEn: The suppression ended in a Han victory. The allied forces of Zheng Ce and Zheng E collapsed after the fighting along the Luocheng and Jiuzhen line; the Han pursued them to the ground around Langjing, Huangbo and Miling, destroyed the main body of the rebel army between the hills and the river valleys, and drove the remnants into the forest. The historical texts record that Zheng E killed herself after the defeat, while the fate of Zheng Ce is recorded as unknown, some sources saying she was taken and others that she spent the rest of her life hidden in the mountains. In the fifth year of Jianyuan (138 BCE) the last resistance inside Jiuzhen was cleared, the commanderies and county offices could be restored, and the campaign ended with Han control of Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Hepu firmly re-established. From the empire's point of view the result was a successful recovery of the frontier: the court won a long-term foothold in the southern interior for a small permanent garrison, and the destruction of Nanyue four years later turned that recovery into a system of commanderies and provinces. From the point of view of Jiaoji's own society the result was the collapse and rebuilding of an older order: the clan-led armed bands were disbanded, the provincial troops were folded into a Han framework, and for the centuries that followed the Han county officials and the southern Yue kinship structures coexisted in Jiaozhi, drawing on one another and also colliding with one another.
